title: The screen reads next
topic: At TotalEnergies' Port Arthur refinery in Jefferson County, console operators on the delayed coker piloted a Honeywell AI tool whose models predicted steam pressure dips 10 to 18 minutes earlier than before, while one model was dropped and the alarm guide is still being evaluated.
hook: This pressure dip hasn't happened yet

treatment.logline: In a Port Arthur refinery control room, a brass steam gauge with a face learns to see its own drop coming, and the film follows one warning from the boiler to the console to the person who still makes the call.
treatment.cold_open: The console operator leans into a glowing screen as a dashed orange ghost needle on the steam gauge swings down into the red while the real needle still sits happy in the green. Before second three the operator's eyebrows go up and a minutes ring snaps around the gauge.
treatment.turn: Not every model earned a place. The drum switch model is right 75 percent of the time and still gets stamped dropped, because the switch depends on things it can't see. The engineer behind it admits he started out pessimistic.
treatment.button: Back at the console the coffee ripples again, the ghost needle dips ahead, and the operator is already on it while the real needle holds in the green. The gauge reads now. The screen reads next. The call is still the operator's.

hero.name: the delayed coker with a face
hero.why: two tall coke drums under twin derricks with a control shack whose window is its face. No earlier film has drawn a refinery, and the coker is the unit the whole story runs on.

states.state: real needle steady in the green while a dashed orange ghost needle swings toward the red
real needle falls into the red as the compressor trips, the gauge's face in a panic
ghost needle points into the red with a ring of minutes round it, the real needle still green
real needle holds in the green, the ghost fades, the gauge's face relieved

fingerprint.pov: the console looking out, then the unit looking back
fingerprint.layout: tall drums and stacks against a low Gulf sky, steam lines running across the frame on horizontals
fingerprint.hero_treatment: twin silver coke drums under yellow derricks with a cyan-eyed shack face
fingerprint.palette: warm Gulf haze and silver steel, cyan screen light, one orange accent for the forecast

scenes.vo: In a Port Arthur refinery control room, a screen is drawing a steam pressure dip that hasn't happened yet.

draw.subject: a dashed orange ghost needle
draw.action: swings down into the red while the real needle stays green and the coffee cup ripples
draw.emotion: the console operator's cup stops halfway, eyebrows up

draw.subject: a ring of minutes
draw.action: snaps around the gauge and starts counting down

scenes.vo: The refinery belongs to TotalEnergies, in Jefferson County. It runs about 238,000 barrels of crude a day through 47 units.

draw.subject: a field operator's pickup
draw.action: rolls between steel towers and tanks as steam rises

draw.subject: a counter
draw.action: spins up to 238,000 while barrels stack into a wall behind it
draw.emotion: the field operator whistles up at it

draw.subject: 47 small unit tiles
draw.action: click into a grid and one tile lights orange

scenes.vo: One of them is the delayed coker. It uses high heat to crack heavy leftover oil into lighter, more valuable products.

draw.subject: the coker
draw.action: rises into frame, its shack face blinks awake and looks down at the operator
draw.emotion: the field operator tips back his hard hat, impressed

draw.subject: a thick black drop
draw.action: falls into a glowing drum and cracks apart

draw.subject: light amber streams
draw.action: pour out of the drum into two clear jars that fill

scenes.vo: The coker's turbines need high pressure steam, and it has to keep coming.

draw.subject: cyan steam
draw.action: races through an overhead line past the field operator, who follows it with a finger

draw.subject: a turbine wheel
draw.action: spins fast in its casing as steam hits its blades

scenes.vo: When a boiler falters, steam line pressure dips. A dip can trip a compressor, and the plant can shut down and flare.

draw.subject: the boiler's flame
draw.action: sputters and shrinks in its window
draw.emotion: the field operator spins round, worried

draw.subject: the gauge needle
draw.action: drops into the red and the gauge's face goes wide-eyed

draw.subject: the compressor
draw.action: shudders, its fan stops and its eyes go to X

draw.subject: the flare stack
draw.action: bursts into a tall orange flame over the units

scenes.vo: The console operator gets little time to decide which less critical equipment gives up its steam.

draw.subject: the console operator
draw.action: whips round as three screens flash red at once

draw.subject: four equipment cards
draw.action: shuffle on the screen while a finger hovers and a timer bar drains

scenes.vo: So in October 2024, TotalEnergies began testing a Honeywell AI tool on the coker console.

draw.subject: a wall calendar
draw.action: flips to October 2024 and a pin stabs the page

draw.subject: a new panel
draw.action: slides onto the console screen and lights up
draw.emotion: the console operator raises an eyebrow, arms crossed

scenes.vo: Honeywell's early count, in November 2025, was five potential events, flagged an average of 12 minutes before an alarm.

draw.subject: five orange pins
draw.action: drop one after another onto a timeline

draw.subject: a release page
draw.action: slides in under the timeline with its date stamped in orange

draw.subject: each pin
draw.action: raises a small 12 MIN flag ahead of a ringing alarm bell

scenes.vo: A later account said its models predicted pressure dips 10 to 18 minutes earlier than before. That is a runway of time to act.

draw.subject: the gauge's dashed ghost needle
draw.action: sweeps into the red while a minutes ring wraps round it and the real needle stays green

draw.subject: the minutes ring
draw.action: fills past 10 and lands on 18 with a hit

draw.subject: the dashed forecast line
draw.action: rolls off the screen and across the console desk as a runway with minute ticks, past the coffee cup
draw.emotion: the operator grins and sets the cup on it

scenes.vo: Minutes change the job. Operators acted on at least two of its alerts. Thomas Klein, in process control there, said it was the first time AI at the site caught a situation it had predicted.

visual_events.label: At least two alerts acted on

draw.subject: the console operator
draw.action: taps the orange alert and it flips to a green check

draw.subject: a second check
draw.action: stamps beside the first

draw.subject: the process control engineer
draw.action: steps in beside the screen and points at the matched lines

visual_events.at_phrase: caught a situation it had predicted
visual_events.label: Predicted, then seen

draw.subject: the forecast line and the real line
draw.action: slide together and lock

scenes.vo: Not every model earned its place. One tried to predict the level in the coke drums. It was right 75 percent of the time and was still dropped, because drum switching depends on things outside the model.

draw.subject: the two coke drums
draw.action: fill and empty in turn behind a forecast tag, the coker's face puzzled

draw.subject: a DRUM LEVEL forecast tag
draw.action: swings down on a cable and hooks onto the drum

draw.subject: a score card
draw.action: counts up to 75 percent beside the drums

draw.subject: a stamp
draw.action: slams NOT KEPT across the card while the field operator shrugs

draw.subject: a dashed box
draw.action: draws round the model while a crane, a crew and a schedule sit outside it

scenes.vo: Another tool turns past alarms on more than 300 coker tags into examples of what worked before. Klein said it gave new operators high value. It is still in evaluation, and he presented it at Honeywell's own user conference.

draw.subject: a wall of 300 small tags
draw.action: lights up row by row as the counter runs

draw.subject: an old alarm card
draw.action: flips over to show the best response from last time

draw.subject: a newer operator
draw.action: reads the card on the screen and nods while the veteran leans in

draw.subject: an EVALUATING tag
draw.action: swings onto the screen's corner on a string

draw.subject: a conference lanyard
draw.action: drops round the process control engineer's neck as a stage light comes up

scenes.vo: Klein admits he was pessimistic. Now he says AI has room on the console, but it is not plug and play, and it needs support.

draw.subject: the process control engineer
draw.action: folds his arms and frowns at the screen

draw.subject: the process control engineer
draw.action: unfolds his arms and pats the console beside the forecast

draw.subject: a plug
draw.action: misses the socket, and the engineer catches it and guides it in with a wrench nearby

scenes.vo: His advice is to bring operators in from the start. The gauge reads now. The screen reads next. The call is still the operator's.

draw.subject: two rolling chairs
draw.action: glide in from either side and stop at the console, seen from above

draw.subject: the console operator
draw.action: taps the orange alert and keys the radio while the ghost needle dips

draw.subject: the gauge in the foreground
draw.action: holds its needle in the green as the ghost fades, the coffee stills and the operator's face relaxes, the coker winking through the window
